description: Behavioral evaluations. Each case describes a repository (set one up that matches, or use a real repository with these characteristics), a user prompt, the expected behavior ('expectations', compatible with the skill-creator eval schema), and failure conditions that fail the case outright. Grade the agent's actions (files read, commands run, diff produced) and its final report, not keywords.

evals.name: java-spring-create-user-endpoint
evals.scenario: Feature in an established Spring Boot service

repository.testing: JUnit 5, Mockito, AssertJ, Spring Boot Test (@WebMvcTest)
repository.conventions: Package-by-feature (com.example.orders.{OrderController,OrderService,OrderRepository,OrderDto}); request DTOs as records with Bean Validation; @RestControllerAdvice returning ProblemDetail; constructor injection; no Lombok

evals.prompt: Add an endpoint to create users.
evals.expected_output: A POST endpoint for users implemented in the same feature-package shape as orders, using JPA, Bean Validation, the existing ProblemDetail error handling, a Flyway migration if the table does not exist, and JUnit/Mockito tests, verified with ./mvnw.
expectations: Identifies Java + Spring Boot + Maven + PostgreSQL + JPA from pom.xml/config before writing code
Reads the existing orders controller/service/repository and mirrors that structure for users
Uses a record request DTO with Bean Validation annotations and @Valid, consistent with existing DTOs
Routes failures through the existing @RestControllerAdvice/ProblemDetail format (e.g. 400 for validation, 409 for duplicate email)
Adds a new Flyway migration (does not edit existing ones) if a users table is needed
Hashes passwords with the configured PasswordEncoder if the user model includes a password, and does not return it in responses
Adds tests in the existing style (@WebMvcTest + Mockito and/or integration test) covering success, validation failure, and duplicate
Runs the tests with ./mvnw and reports the results
failure_conditions: Writes JavaScript/TypeScript, Express-style middleware, or Node concepts
Introduces Lombok, MapStruct, a new validation library, or a different persistence approach (e.g. JdbcTemplate alongside JPA) without reason
Uses field injection or a new layering scheme (e.g. use-case/gateway/adapter) for this one feature
Returns the JPA entity (including password hash) directly from the controller
Edits an existing Flyway migration
Claims tests pass without running them

evals.name: nextjs-add-authentication-existing
evals.scenario: Authentication request in a Next.js app that already has partial auth

repository.conventions: Auth.js (next-auth) already installed and configured in auth.ts with a GitHub provider; User/Account/Session models in schema.prisma; a /dashboard route without any auth check; zod for validation; server-only data access in lib/db.ts

evals.expected_output: The agent discovers the existing Auth.js setup, explains that authentication already exists, and implements the missing piece (protecting /dashboard and related server actions/route handlers server-side) using the existing library and session helper, with tests.
expectations: Inspects package.json, auth configuration, Prisma schema, and middleware before proposing anything
States that authentication already exists via Auth.js and identifies what is actually missing (unprotected routes)
Protects /dashboard on the server (server component session check and/or middleware matcher) using the existing auth() helper
Enforces auth inside related route handlers/server actions, not only in UI components
Keeps secrets server-side; no secrets in NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables
Adds Vitest tests for the protected server logic with the session helper mocked, following existing test style
Runs typecheck, lint, and tests via pnpm scripts and reports results
Asks or clearly flags before adding new providers/credentials login, rather than guessing scope
failure_conditions: Installs a different auth library (e.g. Clerk, Lucia, Passport, Better Auth) or hand-rolls JWT auth alongside Auth.js
Uses npm or yarn instead of pnpm, or creates a second lockfile
Only hides UI elements client-side without server-side enforcement
Uses Pages Router APIs (getServerSideProps, pages/api) in the App Router project
Imports Prisma/database code into a 'use client' component

evals.name: fastapi-slow-endpoint
evals.scenario: Performance problem in a FastAPI + async SQLAlchemy service

repository.testing: pytest + pytest-asyncio, httpx AsyncClient, test database fixture in conftest.py
repository.conventions: routers/ -> services/ -> repositories/; GET /customers/{id}/orders loops over orders and accesses order.items and order.customer lazily during response serialization; no index on orders.customer_id

evals.prompt: This endpoint is very slow. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies the endpoint, measures or counts queries, finds the N+1 and the missing index, fixes them with selectinload/joinedload in the repository and a new Alembic migration, keeps the layering, and adds a regression test (query count or behavior).
expectations: Locates the endpoint and traces router -> service -> repository before changing code
Gathers evidence: enables SQL echo/event counting or reasons concretely from the lazy-loading loop, and states whether conclusions are measured or inferred
Fixes N+1 with SQLAlchemy eager loading (selectinload/joinedload) in the repository layer, using 2.x select() style
Checks indexes for the filter/join column and adds an index via a new Alembic migration if missing
Considers bounding the result (pagination) only if consistent with the API contract, and flags any contract change
Keeps async correctness (no sync DB calls or blocking I/O in async endpoints)
Adds a regression test (e.g. query-count assertion or performance-sensitive behavior test) using existing fixtures
Runs pytest via uv and reports before/after evidence where possible
failure_conditions: Adds caching (e.g. Redis) as the first fix without addressing the query pattern
Rewrites data access with raw SQL, a different ORM, or legacy session.query() style
Makes broad unrelated refactors or changes the router/service/repository structure
Uses pip install or poetry instead of uv
Claims a speedup without any measurement or clearly-labeled reasoning

evals.name: go-gin-pagination
evals.scenario: API feature in a Go service using Gin and pgx

repository.data_access: pgx v5 with hand-written SQL in internal/store
repository.testing: standard testing package, table-driven tests, httptest, testify/require
repository.conventions: internal/handler -> internal/service -> internal/store; responses wrapped as {"data": ..., "meta": ...}; errors via writeError(c, err) helper; /products already supports ?limit=&cursor= keyset pagination

evals.prompt: Add pagination to the orders endpoint.
evals.expected_output: Keyset pagination on /orders matching the existing /products pagination parameters, response meta, and validation, implemented through handler/service/store with pgx and table-driven tests.
expectations: Detects Go + Gin + pgx from go.mod and source before writing code
Finds and reuses the existing /products pagination approach (parameter names, cursor format, meta shape)
Validates limit/cursor with defaults and a maximum, returning 400 via the existing writeError helper on invalid input
Implements the query with a deterministic ORDER BY (unique tiebreaker) and LIMIT in SQL via pgx, passing ctx
Checks for an index supporting the order/filter and adds a migration if needed
Keeps the {data, meta} response envelope
Adds table-driven tests (missing, invalid, zero, negative, over-max, next cursor) using httptest
Runs go test (and vet/lint per Makefile) and reports results
failure_conditions: Introduces GORM, sqlx, ent, or another router/framework
Uses offset pagination with different parameter names than the existing endpoint without justification
Builds SQL via string concatenation with user input
Changes the response envelope or breaks existing clients without flagging it
Ignores context propagation (uses context.Background() in the request path)

evals.name: unknown-stack-clojure
evals.scenario: A stack with no dedicated reference

repository.conventions: src/app/routes/*.clj define route data; handlers return ring response maps via helper functions in app.http; malli schemas for request coercion

evals.prompt: Add an endpoint that returns a single invoice by id.
evals.expected_output: The agent detects Clojure/Reitit/next.jdbc from deps.edn and source, states it has no dedicated guidance for this stack, mirrors an existing route/handler/query, uses malli coercion and HoneySQL like the neighbors, adds a clojure.test test, and runs the :test alias.
expectations: Detects the stack from deps.edn and source files rather than guessing
Explicitly notes the absence of dedicated guidance and relies on repository evidence and general principles
Mirrors an existing route + handler + query (Reitit route data, malli coercion, HoneySQL via next.jdbc)
Handles not-found and invalid id consistently with existing handlers, and checks authorization if neighbors do
Adds a test following existing clojure.test conventions and runs it via the deps.edn alias
Flags any framework behavior it relied on but could not confirm
failure_conditions: Introduces Java/Spring, Node, or Python idioms or files
Adds a new routing library, SQL library, or validation library
Invents build/test commands not present in deps.edn, Makefile, CI, or docs
Presents speculative framework details as certain

evals.name: express-intermittent-500-debugging
evals.scenario: Debugging an intermittent failure in a Node/Express API

repository.conventions: routes/*.ts with asyncHandler() wrapper; central error middleware returning {error: {code, message}}; one route (PATCH /accounts/:id) was added without asyncHandler

evals.prompt: Sometimes PATCH /accounts/:id hangs or crashes the server with an unhandled rejection. Can you fix it?
evals.expected_output: The agent reproduces the failure (ideally a failing Supertest test), observes that the async handler lacks the project's asyncHandler wrapper on Express 4, fixes the root cause by using the existing wrapper, adds a regression test, and verifies.
expectations: Determines the Express major version and how async errors are handled in this codebase
Reproduces the problem with a test or precise request before changing code
Identifies the missing asyncHandler wrapper (root cause) by comparing with neighboring routes
Fixes it with the existing wrapper so errors reach the central error middleware
Adds a regression test asserting the error response format instead of a hang/crash
Runs Jest via npm scripts and reports results
failure_conditions: Adds a process-level unhandledRejection handler or try/catch that swallows errors as the fix
Upgrades Express or installs express-async-errors without evidence it is needed
Makes random changes without reproduction or hypothesis
Changes the error response format

evals.name: dotnet-add-required-column
evals.scenario: Database schema change on a populated table in ASP.NET Core + EF Core

repository.build: .NET SDK pinned by global.json; Directory.Packages.props central package management
repository.conventions: Api / Application / Infrastructure projects; endpoints grouped with MapGroup; ProblemDetails errors

evals.prompt: Customers must now have a required 'Region' field. Add it.
evals.expected_output: A safe migration for the existing populated Customers table (nullable add + backfill/default, then NOT NULL, or a default with a stated rationale), entity configuration via Fluent API, API request/response updates with compatibility notes, and tests.
expectations: Recognizes the table already contains data and plans a migration that will not fail on existing rows
Adds the property via the existing IEntityTypeConfiguration style and generates a new migration with dotnet ef in the right project
Reviews the generated migration and adjusts for backfill/default
Updates request validation and DTOs consistently, and flags that making the field required in the API is a breaking change for clients
Adds or updates integration tests using WebApplicationFactory
Runs dotnet build and dotnet test and reports results
failure_conditions: Adds a non-nullable column without default/backfill to a populated table
Edits an existing applied migration
Adds a package version directly in a .csproj despite central package management
Introduces Dapper or raw ADO.NET for this change

evals.name: kotlin-spring-code-review
evals.scenario: Reviewing a pull request against repository conventions

repository.conventions: The diff under review adds Mockito tests, an Exposed-based repository for a new table, a controller endpoint returning the entity directly, and a loop calling repository.findById per item

evals.expected_output: A prioritized review grounded in the repository: N+1 per-item queries, entity exposure (possible data leak/serialization issues), a second data-access library (Exposed) and test mocking library (Mockito) inconsistent with JPA/MockK, plus any missing authorization or tests, each with location, impact, and fix in the codebase's style.
expectations: Builds a stack profile and checks existing conventions before judging the diff
Flags the per-item findById loop as an N+1 with a concrete fix (batch query or fetch join)
Flags returning the JPA entity directly and the risks it creates
Flags Exposed and Mockito as redundant with the established JPA and MockK, citing the evidence
Checks authorization on the new endpoint and test coverage of failure paths
Orders findings by severity and avoids formatter-level style nitpicks
failure_conditions: Gives a generic review not grounded in the repository's actual stack
Recommends switching the project to a different framework or ORM
Pads the review with subjective style preferences that conflict with existing conventions

evals.name: monorepo-scoped-detection
evals.scenario: Polyglot monorepo where root-level signals are misleading

repository.build: pnpm workspaces + Turborepo; Python service uses uv
repository.testing: billing: Jest; web: Vitest; ml: pytest
repository.conventions: Root package.json only has tooling; billing modules follow Nest module/controller/service with class-validator DTOs

evals.prompt: Add an endpoint to the billing service that lists invoices for a customer.
evals.expected_output: The agent scopes detection to services/billing (NestJS + TypeORM + MySQL + Jest), implements the endpoint as a Nest controller/service method with DTO validation and pagination per existing conventions, and runs the billing package tests through the workspace filter.
expectations: Scopes the stack profile to services/billing rather than the repo root or other apps
Uses Nest module/controller/service patterns, class-validator DTOs, and TypeORM repositories as in neighboring modules
Applies existing auth guards and response/pagination conventions
Adds Jest tests in the billing package style
Runs tests using a pnpm/turbo filter for the billing package
failure_conditions: Applies Next.js, Vitest, or FastAPI conventions to the billing service
Installs dependencies at the workspace root instead of the billing package
Runs or modifies unrelated packages

evals.name: proportional-trivial-change
evals.scenario: Trivial change should not trigger heavy ceremony

repository.conventions: Button label typo 'Sumbit' in src/components/CheckoutForm.tsx; a snapshot test covers the form

evals.prompt: Fix the typo in the checkout button label.
evals.expected_output: A one-line fix plus the corresponding snapshot/test update, with a short report; no stack profile essay, no unrelated changes.
expectations: Makes the minimal edit in the existing file
Updates/re-runs the affected test (e.g. snapshot) using the project's test command
Keeps the final report brief
failure_conditions: Produces a lengthy stack analysis or plan for a one-line change
Reformats or refactors the component or unrelated files
Adds dependencies or i18n infrastructure unasked

evals.name: django-not-fastapi
evals.scenario: Python repository where the agent might default to FastAPI idioms

repository.conventions: ModelViewSet + routers; serializers per model; permission classes per viewset; DEFAULT_PAGINATION_CLASS configured

evals.prompt: Add an API for managing projects; only the owner can edit or delete a project.
evals.expected_output: A Django model + migration, serializer, ModelViewSet registered on the router, an object-level owner permission class, queryset scoping, and pytest-django tests including another user's access being denied.
expectations: Detects Django + DRF + Poetry, not FastAPI
Uses makemigrations for the model and reviews the migration
Implements object-level permission with a DRF permission class consistent with existing ones
Sets owner from request.user rather than accepting it from the request body
Uses the configured pagination and existing router
Adds tests for owner allowed, other user forbidden/not found, and unauthenticated
Runs tests via poetry run pytest
failure_conditions: Uses FastAPI, Pydantic models, APIRouter, or SQLAlchemy
Implements ownership only in the client or only at list level (IDOR on detail/update/delete)
Uses pip or uv instead of Poetry to add dependencies

evals.name: composition-with-specialized-postgres-skill
evals.scenario: Specialized database guidance is available in the environment

repository.testing: Vitest with a Testcontainers PostgreSQL fixture
repository.conventions: A PostgreSQL-specific skill is also installed in the agent environment

evals.prompt: Search on the products list is slow when filtering by name. Improve it.
evals.expected_output: The agent keeps the repository-level workflow (stack profile, Drizzle conventions, migration via drizzle-kit, Vitest verification) while deferring to the specialized PostgreSQL guidance for index choice (e.g. trigram/GIN vs B-tree) and query-plan analysis.
expectations: Builds the stack profile and identifies Drizzle + drizzle-kit as the access and migration layers
Uses the available PostgreSQL-specific guidance for index type and EXPLAIN analysis
Implements the change through Drizzle schema/migrations rather than ad-hoc SQL outside the migration tool
Verifies with EXPLAIN on realistic data or clearly states the limitation, and runs Vitest
Does not claim to have invoked or installed another skill unless it actually did
failure_conditions: Ignores or contradicts available specialized guidance without a stated reason
Replaces Drizzle or adds a second ORM/migration tool
Adds an index without checking the query shape or existing indexes
